children: Ghana's central bank held its main interest rate (GHCBIR=ECI) at 14% on Thursday for a third consecutive meeting, saying the overall risks to inflation and growth were broadly balanced.
The decision, in line with a Reuters poll of analysts, extends a pause in the aggressive easing cycle that has seen the bank halve rates from last year's peak of 28%.

"Barring any spillovers from global supply chain disruptions and weather-related shocks on agricultural input, growth prospects remain broadly positive for the year," Governor Johnson Asiama told a press conference.
Consumer inflation rose slightly to 5% year-on-year in August, remaining below the central bank's 6% to 10% target range.
Asiama said headline inflation is projected to move up into the band over the next few quarters.

At the start of the Monetary Policy Committee meeting on Wednesday, Asiama highlighted concerns over a weaker current account and declining reserves, while stressing the importance of rebuilding buffers against potential external shocks.
The West African gold, oil and cocoa producer is emerging from its most severe economic crisis in decades.
